decisions.reason: Census condition is dead/fallen. No felling permit required to remove a dead tree, and no ecological loss.
decisions.statutory_basis: Not applicable — removal of a dead tree.

decisions.reason: Ficus religiosa at 10 cm obstructs the footprint and exceeds the transplant ceiling (45 cm), so relocation is not reliable. Compensation is age-equivalent, estimated 3-8 saplings. Species is treated as native so the native-conservative branch applies.
decisions.statutory_basis: Maharashtra (Urban Areas) Protection of Trees Act 1975, s.7 — compensation is trees planted in number equal to the AGE of the tree felled. Age is estimated from girth here; the census has no age column.

decisions.reason: Pongamia pinnata at 10 cm obstructs the footprint and exceeds the transplant ceiling (45 cm), so relocation is not reliable. Compensation is age-equivalent, estimated 3-8 saplings. Species is treated as native so the native-conservative branch applies.
decisions.statutory_basis: Maharashtra (Urban Areas) Protection of Trees Act 1975, s.7 — compensation is trees planted in number equal to the AGE of the tree felled. Age is estimated from girth here; the census has no age column.

decisions.reason: Polyalthia longifolia at 46 cm is a confirmed non-native species obstructing the footprint. Statutory compensation is 14-38 saplings, identical to what a native of the same girth would require — but the recommended mix is native-weighted, so the replanting is not simply more Subabul.
decisions.statutory_basis: Maharashtra (Urban Areas) Protection of Trees Act 1975, s.7 — compensation is age-equivalent and SPECIES-BLIND. The statutory count is identical for a native and a non-native tree. This tool applies the same count to both and expresses the native/non-native distinction in the recommended species mix instead, which is the ecologically meaningful lever and stays inside the Act.

decisions.reason: Ficus racemosa at 68 cm obstructs the footprint and exceeds the transplant ceiling (45 cm), so relocation is not reliable. Compensation is age-equivalent, estimated 21-56 saplings. Species is treated as native so the native-conservative branch applies.
decisions.statutory_basis: Maharashtra (Urban Areas) Protection of Trees Act 1975, s.7 — compensation is trees planted in number equal to the AGE of the tree felled. Age is estimated from girth here; the census has no age column.

decisions.reason: Girth 110 cm at or above the 90 cm house-policy heritage threshold. Relocation is not realistic at this size; design should be adjusted to retain the tree.
decisions.statutory_basis: HOUSE POLICY (not the 1975 Act) — the Act requires Tree Officer permission, with no girth-based automatic prohibition.

recommendations.action: Reduce impervious cover by 18 percentage points (permeable paving, green roof, or open landscape)
Substitute 35% of each material with its lower-carbon alternative
Redesign the footprint to retain the 1 heritage-class trees on site, recovering 50 m2 of canopy
recommendations.composite_tradeoff: green 99.2 -> 98.7 (improves by 0.5), but carbon intensity rises 13.2 -> 14.3 because the same materials are spread over a smaller footprint. Composite impact moves +0.1.
recommendations.note: Canopy preserved rather than replaced. Saplings do not substitute for retained mature canopy on any useful timescale.

recommendations.verification_note: Each 'delta' is a genuine re-run of the deterministic scorer on the modified site. Recommendations that did not move the score are dropped, not reported.
